newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLAR SWITCHES 3 SCHIPHOL FLIGHTS TO PRESTWICK.
newsitem.headline: POLAR SWITCHES 3 SCHIPHOL FLIGHTS TO PRESTWICK.

text.p: Polar Air Cargo, became the first carrier to divert flights from Schiphol due to the Dutch airport's new and widely critcised night-time ban on noisy aircraft.

Jacques Heeremans, director of Inter Aviation Services, the Dutch general sales agent for Polar Air, told Reuters that three of its seven weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flights will from today go via Glasgow's Prestwick airport instead of Amsterdam.

But he added that the Long Beach-based carrier will try to keep one of the three flights at Schiphol if the scheduling allows it to turn around before the time at which the night ban comes into operation.

"We are in the process of readjusting all of our schedules so if it is possible to have one of these flights call at Prestwick and then continue on to Schiphol and turn around, we will keep Prestwick as a buffer for Schiphol."
The flights involved fly on to both the U.S. and Asia.
"It is a costly exercise, we do not want to have to do it but we have no choice," said Heeremans.

The ban which took effect on August 5 prevents noisier aircraft such as McDonnell Douglas DC-10 and Boeing 747 in its 100,200,300 and SP versions from taking-off between 2300 and 0600 local (2100 and 0400 gmt) hours, in a bid reduce noise levels.
A spokesman from Polar Air's handler at Schiphol, Aero Groundservices B.V., said that the U.S. airline's said the flight cutbacks were "a big blow ".
Israeli carrier El Al is also handled by Aerground and is also expected to move its cargo operations to another airport,industry sources said.
They added that in the longer term the carrier may move its whole operation from Schiphol to Ostend or Liege as noise measures get tougher at Schiphol.

Heeremans said that if the new government measures make it impossible to continue operations, the carrier will have no choice and have to relocate. "We are looking at all of the possibilities," he said.

Polar began its UK operations at Prestwick in 1993 but flights were transferred to London Heathrow. On August 4 Polar announced from Long Beach that it was returning to Prestwick due to demand from U.S. shipper demand for driect services to Scotland while offering beyond services to Amsterdam and New Delhi. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
